findings.check: unrepaired option-level English flag (fresh G-ENG round) — belongs to the adjudication package
findings.quote: It is heaviest on the aids moored inshore, where the channel water is narrow.
findings.note: Q1 option D, flagged class 3 at minor by two of the three fresh legs independently, both naming the same rewrite ('where the channel is narrow'). Leg 1: '"the channel water is narrow" is not an English collocation — the passage's own "where the water is narrow" works because "narrow water(s)" is fixed trade idiom, but premodifying it with "channel" makes a compound noun of which "narrow" cannot naturally be predicated'. Leg 3: 'noun-stacked "channel water" is an awkward pairing - a channel is narrow, water is shallow'. Student-facing English in an English-comprehension item, so it is real; minor on the gate's own grounds because it is a distractor rather than a key and the item is unaffected either way (D is wrong_location regardless, and the Q1 rationale grounds itself on the passage's own correct 'inshore aids, where the water is narrow'). regate_status now lists it among the surviving minors, so it is on the ledger rather than lost.

findings.quote: In flat water a lift, a scrape, a fresh lamp and a relay take about forty minutes.
findings.note: Carried unchanged; no repair round has touched it. The narrated job runs from 'At twenty past six the crane on the Marram takes the weight' to 'By nine o'clock buoy 43 has a scraped skirt, a new lamp and eleven fresh links at the swivel' — about two hours forty against a stated forty minutes. Defensible rather than false ('In flat water' is an explicit hedge, 'eleven fresh links at the swivel' is chainwork beyond the four listed steps, 'by nine o'clock' is an upper bound), but the text never reconciles the two figures and no gate or review has recorded the tension. Downstream-inert: the only rationale that touches it is Q5's WHY-KEY, listing 'the forty-minute turnaround' among the craft details.

findings.quote: C states exactly that, and no more
findings.note: Carried unchanged. The passage clause is 'so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart'; the key says 'It may be riding the edge of the circle its chain allows'. 'The edge' is one notch tighter than 'somewhere inside', and no clause licenses the perimeter specifically. C remains clearly best — the stem stipulates a buoy 'found some way from the position printed on the chart', so the outer part of the circle is the natural reading, 'may be' hedges it, all four post-repair G-KEY legs solved C, and the fresh G-STEM leg picks C too — but the claim of exact equivalence is stronger than the text supports, and it was introduced by the 2026-08-25 re-grounding rather than inherited. A four-word softening of the rationale closes it; no option or key change is implied.
